nodes.label: Files at a glance
nodes.community_name: Minima Core (Android) — UI redesign + H2 fix

nodes.label: H2 dependency downgrade 2.4.240 -> 2.1.214
nodes.rationale: 2.1.214 is the last H2 2.x release whose SHA256 bytecode verifies cleanly on strict ART builds (e.g. Samsung); minima.jar bundles zero org/h2 classes, so the offending class comes solely from the gradle dependency and a one-line pin is a complete fix. Any future H2 upgrade must be verified on strict ARTs first.

nodes.label: ART VerifyError kills node at boot (H2 2.4.240)
nodes.rationale: Android's ART bytecode verifier rejects H2 2.4.240's SHA256.getPBKDF2; the node opens its H2 DB with a password (ConnectionInfo.hashPassword -> SHA256.getPBKDF2), so the VerifyError kills the node's main thread at boot while the wallet UI hangs on 'Syncing Minima Wallet..' forever.
nodes.norm_label: art verifyerror kills node at boot (h2 2.4.240)

nodes.label: Wallet.signData unsynchronized read-modify-write race
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: signData was the only non-synchronized mutator on Wallet: two concurrent signers both read uses=N, both sign leaf N, both write N+1 — a reused Winternitz one-time signature that leaks the leaf's private key. TreeKey.verify() has no index monotonicity, so the network accepts the reuse. Confirmed in the wild (7 of 64 default keys reused, witness-exact). Only the node can fix it: an app can serialise its own signing but not collisions with a different app on the same key. Fix: make signData and updateUses synchronized (reentrant monitors keep helpers safe), also fixing the non-thread-safe shared PreparedStatements SQL_GET_KEY / SQL_UPDATE_KEY_USES.

nodes.label: sendsign burns a key leaf per input coin
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: reqsigs.add(pubkey) was never called in sendsign.java so the dedupe guards never fired: an N-input send consumed N leaves instead of 1 and appended N duplicate signatures. Subtlety: the burn transaction needs its own dedupe list because it has a different transaction ID, so a key that signed the main txn must still sign the burn.
nodes.norm_label: sendsign burns a key leaf per input coin

nodes.label: MegaMMR import robustness on constrained heaps
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: A 343 MB mainnet mega.mmr needs ~1.3 GB decoded and killed a 512 MB phone heap with no usable error. Four fixes: catch(Throwable) + pre-flight heap check (OOM is an Error, not Exception); stream the IBD in 256-block batches (cascade only in batch #1, restore=true, per-batch isIBDProcessFinished poll, resetFirstIBDTimer to defuse the tip gate); heap watermark max(32MB, 5% of heap) + -megaprune applied at read time (isPrunable is a pure per-coin test); the same watermark every 64k entries in MMR.java because the MMR tree (1,513,769 entries ~ 1.0 GB) is the real ceiling. Practical conclusion: mainnet MegaMMR needs ~1.2 GB heap; on 512 MB phones use -megammr plus -megaprune.
nodes.norm_label: megammr import robustness on constrained heaps

nodes.label: Companion commands off the broadcast main thread
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: onReceive ran commands synchronously on the main thread: socket-opening commands (megammrsync, archive resync) threw NetworkOnMainThreadException, swallowed into a misleading 'Could not connect to Archive host!'. Fix: single-thread ExecutorService keeps ordering strictly serialised; a throwing command now returns status:false instead of failing silently.
nodes.norm_label: companion commands off the broadcast main thread

nodes.label: Large IPC results as content:// file hand-off
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: The response travels as one Intent String extra under two ceilings: the 256,000-char MAX_MESSAGE_LEN stub and the ~1 MB Binder transaction limit (over-limit broadcast throws TransactionTooLargeException in the receiving process, uncatchably) — so the transport itself must change for big payloads. Negotiated per command via CMD_FILERESP=true, three-way compatible with old clients/nodes; oversized results go to cacheDir/ipcresponses/<responseid>.json via a non-exported FileProvider (authority org.minimarex.minimacore.ipcresponses) read-granted to exactly the calling package; a file descriptor crosses Binder, not the data. Files pruned after 5 minutes, wiped at receiver start, failed write falls back to the stub.
nodes.norm_label: large ipc results as content:// file hand-off

nodes.label: Admin-gated FILE bridge (node base-folder access)
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: backup, megammr action:export, txnexport write into the node's private getFilesDir(), unreachable without adb. New broadcast action org.minimarex.minimacore.FILE with list/stat/get/put/mkdir/move/delete. Security model: admin-gated (an admin app can already run backup and read everything, so this is reach-parity, not new privilege); path containment via canonical resolution; write-protected databases/ so a file manager can never corrupt the live wallet/chain DBs. Old nodes lack .FILE in their IntentFilter and ignore it cleanly.

nodes.label: IPC reply cap split — MAX_RESPONSE_LEN 100000
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: MAX_MESSAGE_LEN counts UTF-16 chars but Parcel.writeString serialises ~2 bytes/char: a reply just under 256,000 chars builds a ~512KB parcel and the broadcast queue kills the RECEIVING app at roughly the 256KB-parcel line (TransactionTooLargeException before any callback; diagnostic signature: am_kill 'Can't deliver broadcast'). Observed live twice (2026-08-09, 2026-08-17): a ~131K-char coins reply killed a companion on every launch. Fix: inbound keeps MAX_MESSAGE_LEN 256000 (signing payloads must not regress); both reply sites use MAX_RESPONSE_LEN 100000 (~200KB parcel, safely under the kill line); bigger replies ride the file hand-off or the honest stub. 19 lines in MinimaReceiver.java, commit b326c7ae3f6afe935278d850b7f6d294de84521e (1.6.9-ui-h2).

nodes.label: allowBackup off — node data dir was going to the cloud
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: The app's getFilesDir() IS the Minima node's data directory and main_prefs holds the BIP39 seed in cleartext; the manifest carried the scaffold default allowBackup=true with no backup-rules attributes, so Android Auto Backup uploaded a spendable wallet and its private keys to the user's cloud, and a restore could reconstitute a signing node on any phone — which is also key-reuse territory. Fix: allowBackup=false plus explicit excludes in both backup_rules.xml and data_extraction_rules.xml.
nodes.norm_label: allowbackup off — node data dir was going to the cloud

nodes.label: Runtime Allow Screenshots toggle (FLAG_SECURE)
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: FLAG_SECURE stays the default (screenshots blocked) but becomes a persisted user choice (ALLOW_SCREENSHOTS in main_prefs, bypassed on debuggable builds), applied per-activity from MinimaApplication; default release behaviour unchanged until the user opts in.

nodes.label: Latent -clean boot hazard in extra-params path
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: A stored -clean in minima_extra_params was stripped from the SAVED string, but the ORIGINAL string was tokenized into the boot args — so the wipe ran on the very boot it was set. Branch fix/extra-params-boot-leak.
nodes.norm_label: latent -clean boot hazard in extra-params path

nodes.label: Restyle + navigation: Home/Wallet/Terminal/Apps tabs
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: Resources-only dark-first Material3 restyle with all @ids and view types preserved so Java bindings are untouched; structural redesign keeps Apps at index 3 and the dashboard at index 0 so the MainAdapter.getAppsView() cast and MinimaNewBlock() refresh wiring are untouched; Send/Receive become thin host activities around the UNMODIFIED SendView/ReceiveView.

nodes.label: Wallet token icons + web-validation
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: Remote icon URLs are treated as hostile: byte-bounded LRU-cached async loader, downsampling, SVG via AndroidSVG, and loopback/LAN hosts blocked so token metadata cannot point the app at the local node RPC. A token is validated when the document at its token.webvalidate URL contains the tokenid (domain-ownership proof); deterministic identicon fallback; defensive parsing of the token field in all its shapes.

nodes.label: Truthful numbers, full identifiers, working send
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: Every token row shows sendable (confirmed overstated every balance with contract-locked coins); nothing truncated anywhere — coin ids, token ids, amounts, peer strings all full, Format.shortHash deleted outright, ids must round-trip into 'coins coinid:...' byte for byte; Max fills sendable not confirmed (which would build a failing send); send failures read both 'message' and 'error' keys so the node's precise reason reaches the user; 'Funds Sent!' became 'Transaction posted — mining…' because a send reply means built-and-posted, not on-chain; the NEWBALANCE service event is the honest confirmation point (MinimaNewBalance -> 'Balance updated on chain').
nodes.norm_label: truthful numbers, full identifiers, working send

nodes.label: Startup Params screen
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: Server mode passes exactly one of -server / -isclient (both write IS_ACCEPTING_IN_LINKS and passing both was iteration-order dependent); wipe/seed flags (-clean -genesis -solo -seed -anyseed -dbpassword) and app-managed flags are blocked in the UI; free-text extra args validated with ParamConfigurer.checkParams at save time; wired to the pre-existing minima_extra_params pref the service always consumed but no UI ever set.

nodes.label: Logs tab — live on-device node log tail
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: Zero jar changes: MinimaLogger already posts every line as a MINIMALOG notify event, the app just never consumed it. Bounded 600-line buffer, Pause/Resume/Clear/Share, substring filter, per-subsystem verbosity chips driving the node's own 'logs <key>:true|false' command, chip state seeded from the reply.
nodes.norm_label: logs tab — live on-device node log tail

nodes.label: Family release key + signature-gated IPC receivers
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: Releases signed with a managed 4096-bit RSA family key instead of the debug key, enabling android:protectionLevel=signature gating of the IPC receivers across the app family; upgrading from an older-signed install requires uninstall/reinstall.
nodes.norm_label: family release key + signature-gated ipc receivers

nodes.label: minimaapi.aar client library (MinimaAPI)
nodes.rationale: Android lib letting third-party apps talk to Minima Core: register a MinimaAPIListener, run commands via MinimaAPI.Command(), and call onDestroy() to shut down cleanly; the companion app must be enabled by the user in Minima-Core.

nodes.label: IPC change 1: single-thread ExecutorService in MinimaReceiver
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: MinimaReceiver is registered without a Handler so onReceive runs on the process main thread and calls runMinimaCMD synchronously; socket-opening commands throw NetworkOnMainThreadException which sendArchiveReq's catch-all swallows into a misleading error, plus ANR risk. The executor preserves strict serialisation while moving execution off the main thread; registration/enable/admin checks stay on the receiver thread. Submitted as PR #1; changes 2 and 3 build on it.
nodes.norm_label: ipc change 1: single-thread executorservice in minimareceiver

nodes.label: IPC change 2: content:// file hand-off for large results
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: Raising the 256,000-char MAX_MESSAGE_LEN cap is not an option because the ~1 MB Binder transaction limit sits beneath it and throws TransactionTooLargeException in the receiving process uncatchably — the transport itself has to change for big payloads. Negotiated per command (CMD_FILERESP=true), three-way compatible: old client -> new node gets the byte-identical stub, new client -> old node has the unknown extra ignored, small results keep the inline path with zero overhead. The client library reads the URI off the main thread and delivers through the unchanged MinimaAPIListener.response(JSONObject) — apps need only the updated minimaapi library. Commit 6bcefae; new MinimaAPIMessages constants MINIMA_API_CMD_FILERESP, MINIMA_API_RESPONSE_URI, MINIMA_API_RESPONSE_LEN.
nodes.norm_label: ipc change 2: content:// file hand-off for large results

nodes.label: IPC change 3: admin-gated FILE broadcast action
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: Built for the Filez file manager: a third broadcast action org.minimarex.minimacore.FILE alongside REGISTER and CMD, with FILE_ACTION/FILE_PATH/FILE_NEWPATH/FILE_URI extras and list/stat/get/put/mkdir/move/delete actions. stat resolves paths exactly like MiniFile.createBaseFile and reports canonical ground truth. Admin-gated (reach-parity with an admin app that can already run backup), canonical path containment, write-protected databases/, runs on the change-1 executor, oversized listings use the change-2 hand-off. Commits d681355 and e0b418f.
nodes.norm_label: ipc change 3: admin-gated file broadcast action

nodes.label: Material3 design system in res/ (tokens, Manrope, minima_orange)
nodes.rationale: Colours, type, shapes and component styles are tokens in values/ + values-night/; layouts consume the tokens. Every @id and view type preserved so Java bindings keep working (Button -> MaterialButton is a safe subclass). Fixed a real night-mode bug: values-night on_primary was near-black #12100F making labels on orange buttons unreadable — set to #FFFFFF.
nodes.norm_label: material3 design system in res/ (tokens, manrope, minima_orange)

nodes.label: Tab restructure Home/Wallet/Terminal/Apps (MainAdapter/MainActivity)
nodes.rationale: Two hard constraints respected so service/DB wiring stays untouched: MainAdapter.getAppsView() casts mAllViews[3] so Apps stays index 3; MainActivity.MinimaNewBlock() -> refreshHomeView() refreshes mAllViews[0] so the dashboard stays index 0. HomeView and TerminalView already existed in the tree, just unwired.

nodes.label: SendActivity / ReceiveActivity thin hosts around unmodified views
nodes.rationale: Rather than duplicate any logic, the self-contained SendView/ReceiveView are hosted verbatim in two thin activities (Toolbar + container adding getMainView()); the send command and receive getAddress/QR path are byte-for-byte the originals.
nodes.norm_label: sendactivity / receiveactivity thin hosts around unmodified views

nodes.label: Token icon pipeline: IconResolver/ImageLoader/Identicon/WebValidate/TokenMeta
nodes.rationale: Ported from the utxoWallet / canonical Minima wallet. IconResolver handles <artimage> base64, data: URIs, http(s), inline <svg>, raw base64; ImageLoader is async, byte-bounded, LRU-cached, downsamples to avoid OOM, rasterises SVG via AndroidSVG and blocks loopback/LAN hosts so token metadata can't point the app at the local node RPC; Identicon gives a deterministic 5x5 fallback; WebValidate proves domain ownership by checking the token.webvalidate URL contains the tokenid; TokenMeta defensively parses the token field in all its shapes. New dep com.caverock:androidsvg-aar:1.4.
